rules: Nothing here becomes PASS from code. The agent never invents, reads, shows, logs or commits a password, key, token or DSN.
Secrets go only into the provider dashboard (Supabase Auth/Vault/Edge secrets, GitHub environments). Never into the repo, a report or the APK.
Supersedes the open items of docs/reports/rc2-3-8-owner-actions.md and docs/release/rc2-2-20-owner-actions.json (both kept as history).

actions.title: Add production, Android and preview callback URLs to Supabase Auth redirect allowlist
steps: Supabase dashboard (MandarimProject) -> Auth -> URL Configuration.
Add https://<production host>/auth/callback, longyu.noba.com://auth/callback and each preview host you test.
No secret involved; record the list (hosts only) in the RC2.3.10 report.

actions.title: Configure Google sign-in (Google Cloud OAuth client -> Supabase provider)
steps: Google Cloud Console: OAuth consent screen (external, app name Longyu, support e-mail).
Create a Web OAuth client; authorized redirect URI = the Supabase project auth callback.
Paste client id and secret only into Supabase -> Auth -> Providers -> Google, then enable it.
Never put the secret in the repo, .env files, the APK or a report.

actions.title: Configure Sign in with Apple (Services ID + key -> Supabase provider)
steps: Apple Developer: App ID with Sign in with Apple, a Services ID, return URL = Supabase auth callback.
Create a .p8 key, generate the client secret per Supabase docs, paste only into Supabase -> Auth -> Providers -> Apple.
Calendar a rotation (client secret expires every 6 months).
If you e-mail private-relay addresses, register the sending domain with Apple.
actions.note: Apple Developer Program membership is a paid account; the owner decides whether Apple sign-in is in launch scope.

actions.title: Configure Microsoft sign-in (Entra app registration -> Supabase azure provider)
steps: Microsoft Entra: app registration for personal + organizational accounts (or consumers only).
Redirect URI = Supabase auth callback; add the optional e-mail-verified claim per Supabase docs.
Paste application id and secret (and tenant URL if not common) only into Supabase -> Auth -> Providers -> Azure.

actions.title: List only configured providers in VITE_AUTH_PROVIDERS for Netlify and Android builds
steps: After each provider is enabled, set VITE_AUTH_PROVIDERS (e.g. google,apple,azure - only the configured ones) in Netlify build env and the Android build env.
This is a public list, not a secret. With nothing set the login shows e-mail only.

actions.title: Decide and switch Supabase manual identity linking; confirm the automatic same-verified-e-mail linking policy
steps: Supabase -> Auth -> settings: enable manual linking (beta) if 'Vincular' in Conta should work.
Record the decision on automatic linking for same verified e-mail.
Until enabled, link/unlink stays OWNER_ACTION_REQUIRED.

actions.title: Real Android OAuth test (cold start, warm start, back from browser)
steps: Requires at least one provider configured (OA-AUTH-GOOGLE) and the redirect allowlist (OA-AUTH-REDIRECT-URLS).
Install the current APK; run device matrix rows DM-20-ANDROID-OAUTH-DEEP-LINK and DM-19-SOCIAL-SIGN-IN.
Record device, Android version, APK artifact id, date. No e-mail or token in the notes.

actions.title: Run OWNER_AUTH_ACCEPTANCE (e-mail, social, claim, logout/switch, offline logout)
steps: Run device matrix rows DM-18, DM-19, DM-20, DM-21 from docs/release/owner-acceptance.json.
E-mail rows (DM-18, DM-21) can run now; social rows wait for provider config.

actions.title: Apply the code-based password recovery e-mail template in Supabase
steps: Supabase -> Authentication -> Email Templates -> Reset Password: paste supabase/templates/recovery.html.
Evidence: screenshot without secrets + a received e-mail with a 6-digit code (do not store the code).

actions.title: Owner Hanzi physical acceptance (trace, memory, eligibility lock)
steps: Install the current APK; complete 'Montando primeiros hanzi' first (writing is locked before that by design).
Run DM-11-HANZI-WRITING plus the canvas parts of DM-24-RESUME-LIFECYCLE.
Only then may OWNER_PHYSICAL_PASS be claimed.
actions.note: Was the RC2.3.4A exit criterion; still open.

actions.title: Owner audio and speech acceptance (canonical audio, conversation, contrast, record/playback/compare, torture matrix)
steps: Run DM-06 to DM-10 on a real device with the current APK.
Earlier owner runs on PR #303/#305 builds FAILED; a new run on the current build is required - old results do not carry over.
Speech expansion beyond the 8-item pilot waits for this.
actions.note: Was the RC2.3.5 exit criterion (OWNER_AUDIO_ACCEPTANCE); still open.

actions.title: Owner UX acceptance (first use, answers, completion, navigation, Culture, Visual First, Pedagogy, Personal Mastery)
steps: Run every ux-area row of docs/release/owner-acceptance.json (DM-02..05, DM-12..17, DM-25, DM-26).
Answer the central question from RC2.3.7: one finished experience, or features glued together?
actions.note: Replaces OWNER_PEDAGOGICAL / VISUAL / HUMAN / CULTURE / MASTERY / UX acceptance as separate runs.

actions.title: Owner Android core run (clean install, back, offline, resume, notifications)
steps: Run DM-01, DM-22, DM-23, DM-24, DM-28 with the current APK; record model, Android version, APK artifact id, date.

actions.title: Decide how to reconcile production migration history with the repo
steps: Read docs/reports/rc2-3-9-cloud-handoff.md item CH-01.

Choose: (a) map existing production rows to repo files in a checked-in ledger without touching the database, or (b) repair the history table after an export. (a) is non-destructive and recommended first.
No change to production until OA-DATA-EXPORT and OA-SCHEMA-DIFF are done.
actions.risk: A wrong history repair re-applies or skips migrations.
actions.reason: Ledger: 19 MATCH, 11 UNKNOWN (content differs or placeholder rows such as "select 1; -- applied via execute_sql chunks"), 6 PROD_ONLY, 27 REPO_ONLY.
actions.exactAction: Read docs/launch/production-migration-ledger.json and choose: (a) keep history as-is and treat the ledger as the source of truth (recommended, non-destructive), or (b) a later, separate history repair after OA-DATA-EXPORT and OA-SCHEMA-DIFF.
actions.evidenceExpected: Your choice recorded in the PR (a or b). Nothing else.

actions.title: Run a read-only schema diff production vs repo
steps: From the owner machine: link the CLI to MandarimProject and run a schema-only diff (read-only).
The database password stays on the owner machine; never paste it into a chat, report or CI log.
Attach the diff output (schema only, no data) to the RC2.3.10 report.
actions.reason: Table/function/policy-level diff is done (snapshot read 2026-10-08); a column-level diff needs a schema-only dump from production.
actions.exactAction: On your machine: `npx supabase db dump --linked --schema public --schema-only -f prod-schema.sql` (project drjcfalvlbbeblmmyhwj), then `npx supabase db diff` against a local stack built from supabase/migrations. Keep the dump private; paste only the diff summary (object names) into the PR.

actions.title: Owner-held export / backup before any production migration
steps: Free plan has no backups or PITR.
Before every production migration: schema-only dump + data export of user_progress, subscriptions, economy_ledger (and auth-related tables per Supabase docs).
Store it privately with the owner (not in the repo, not in a public artifact). Record only date + table list + row counts.
actions.risk: A dump contains user data: keep it encrypted and private, never in Git.
actions.exactAction: Follow docs/launch/production-backup-runbook.md §2–§4 (schema-only dump + data export of the critical tables), verify the export with §5, store it encrypted offline.
actions.evidenceExpected: Timestamp, source project ref, candidate SHA and row counts per table (no data) pasted in the PR.

actions.title: Approve raw telemetry retention (e.g. 30 days raw -> daily aggregates)
steps: Decide retention for beta_pedagogy_events and other raw telemetry.
Implementation is a deleting job, so it needs export first and explicit owner approval.
Without it the DB passes 500 MB around 1 000 MAU (audit projection).
actions.reason: beta_pedagogy_events keeps raw rows forever (1 888 rows, 3.0 MB on 2026-10-08); cleanup function exists in production but is not scheduled.
actions.exactAction: Choose A (30 d raw + aggregates, recommended), B (60 d) or C (90 d). supabase/pending/rc2-3-10-telemetry-retention.sql then ships in DRY RUN; switching to real deletes is a separate approved statement.
actions.evidenceExpected: A, B or C written in the PR.

actions.title: Read the usage numbers connectors cannot see
steps: Supabase -> Usage: egress and Edge Function invocations for the current cycle.
Netlify -> Team -> Usage: credits used this cycle (shared by 4 sites).
Paste the numbers (no keys) into docs/launch/platform-budget-registry.json in RC2.3.10.
actions.exactAction: Supabase → Project MandarimProject → Usage: egress and Edge Function invocations this cycle. Netlify → Team → Usage: credits used. Resend → Usage: emails this month. Paste numbers only.

actions.title: Verify a sending domain in Resend
steps: Resend has 0 domains on the free plan (3 allowed).
Add the domain and the DNS records Resend shows at your DNS provider; wait for verification.
Do not create API keys in the repo.

actions.title: Set Resend as Supabase Auth custom SMTP
steps: After OA-RESEND-DOMAIN: create a sending-only Resend API key and paste it only into Supabase -> Auth -> SMTP settings.
Send a test confirmation and a recovery e-mail to a test inbox; record delivery yes/no only.

actions.title: Create the Sentry project and decide on the SDK
steps: Org exists with 0 projects and there is no SDK in the app.
Create one project (browser/React) when RC2.3.10 starts; the DSN goes into build env only.
Sampling per platform-responsibility-map.md (errors 1.0, traces 0.02, session replay 0, replay on error 0.1).
The CSP connect-src in netlify.toml must then allow the Sentry ingest host (code change in RC2.3.10).
actions.exactAction: Create a Sentry project (platform: browser JavaScript), copy the DSN into Netlify env VITE_SENTRY_DSN (production context) and into the Android release env; tell the agent the ingest host (e.g. oXXXX.ingest.us.sentry.io — host only) so connect-src gets exactly that host.
actions.evidenceExpected: Ingest host name + a screenshot description of SENTRY_TEST_EVENT arriving.

actions.title: Confirm the [release]-only production deploy rule
steps: Production deploys only for commits marked [release] (netlify.toml ignore). It goes live on merge.
Confirm this is the intended behaviour before merging the stack.

actions.title: Run the rollback drill once
steps: Netlify: publish a previous deploy and back again; record times.
Database: confirm the 'irreversible - restore from export' note exists for each migration in the release.
actions.exactAction: Netlify → site singular-meringue-7838cd → Deploys: note the published deploy and its version.json SHA; "Publish deploy" on the previous production deploy; open /version.json (must show the older SHA); publish the current one back; open /version.json again.
actions.evidenceExpected: The 4 SHAs/times (current → previous → current) and how long each switch took.
actions.risk: A minute of the previous frontend; no database change.

actions.title: Check TypeSafe/Jev credits and redeploy triage-feedback with the guardrails
steps: Read credits/quota in the TypeSafe console (not readable from the agent container).
After merge, redeploy the triage-feedback Edge Function: production v1 predates the timeout/breaker/dedupe guardrails.
Key stays only in Supabase Vault (TYPESAFE_API_KEY).
actions.reason: Production triage-feedback is v1 (2026-10-07): 8 s timeout, no kill switch, no circuit breaker, no dedupe. Repo version carries all four.
actions.exactAction: (1) TypeSafe console → note remaining credits/quota (number only). (2) After this PR merges: GitHub → Actions → "Deploy Edge Function (manual, from main)" → function triage-feedback, confirm DEPLOY-triage-feedback, expected_sha = merge SHA.
actions.evidenceExpected: Credits number + the workflow run URL (its summary lists the new version).
actions.readOrWrite: write (Edge Function deploy, reversible by redeploying)
actions.risk: Low: admin-only function; previous v1 source is recorded in docs/reports/rc2-3-10-jev-production-certification.md.

actions.title: Confirm which Stripe account backs the Edge Functions and keep live mode off until RC2.3.11
steps: Connected account shows test mode only, 0 products, 0 webhooks.
Confirm in the Supabase Edge secrets page (names only) which account the checkout/webhook functions use.
Create no live products before the RC2.3.11 pricing decision.

actions.title: Record the Google Play billing compliance decision for Brazil before any in-APK checkout
steps: Audit current Play policy (Play Billing, alternative/user-choice billing, external links, fees) for digital educational subscriptions in Brazil.
Technically working is not the same as allowed.

actions.title: Confirm Play developer identity, package registration and package name longyu.noba.com
steps: Play Console: confirm developer verification status, package registration, and that the app shows package longyu.noba.com.
If another package appears: do not upload, do not create a second app.

actions.title: Create the upload key, back it up twice, store passwords, configure GitHub environment secrets
steps: Run the keystore init script on the owner machine with a path outside the repo; keytool asks for passwords in your terminal.
Two offline backups in different places; passwords in your password manager.
GitHub -> Settings -> Environments -> android-release: add the secrets (record names only, never values).
Record only the PUBLIC SHA-256 fingerprint of the upload certificate.

actions.title: First signed AAB, Play App Signing, internal track upload, install from Play, N -> N+1
steps: Signed AAB from the release workflow; enable Play App Signing (Google-managed key).
Create the internal track, upload, install from Play (sideload does not count).
Repeat critical device rows on the Play build; then ship N+1 and verify the update keeps progress (DM-27).

actions.title: Store listing assets (feature graphic, final phone screenshots)
steps: Produce the feature graphic and final phone screenshots from the release build.

actions.title: Approve the schema-diff + export runbook for the first controlled production migration (#273)
steps: #273 stays open until every RC2.3.10 row in docs/launch/rc2-3-10-cloud-handoff.json is PASS.
Approve Option B (single cloud project + local Supabase/CI QA); no paid plan, no pause/delete of the sibling project.

actions.title: Retarget #314 base from main to cursor/rc2-3-3-culture-deep-journey-25db (it already contains #309–#313; merging it first would land them unreviewed)
steps: On GitHub, edit PR #314 and change its base branch from main to cursor/rc2-3-3-culture-deep-journey-25db.
Confirm the diff now shows only #314's own commits.
Merge the stack bottom-up, never #314 first.
actions.note: Moot: #320 converged the whole stack on main (ec26ffc) and #321 followed (7d1890a). No retarget left to do.

actions.title: Prove which commit is live on the production site
actions.reason: This agent session cannot reach *.netlify.app (egress policy) and Netlify posts no commit status on main, so the live SHA is unproven — including whether the [release] deploy of ec26ffc happened.
actions.exactAction: Open https://singular-meringue-7838cd.netlify.app/version.json and copy commitSha, curriculumFingerprint and buildChannel. If commitSha is not a main SHA after ec26ffc, the [release] deploy did not run: Netlify → Deploys → check the build log for "[netlify-ignore]".

actions.title: Confirm Edge Function secret NAMES (no values)
actions.reason: The MCP cannot list Edge secrets. create-account honors TURNSTILE_ALLOW_SKIP=1 when the Turnstile secret is missing; it must not exist in production.
actions.exactAction: Supabase → Edge Functions → Secrets: list the NAMES. TURNSTILE_ALLOW_SKIP must be absent. Note whether JEV_DEV_AUDIT_ENABLED / JEV_RUNTIME_ENABLED / TYPESAFE_API_KEY / TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY are set as Edge secrets (Vault already holds TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY and TYPESAFE_API_KEY).

actions.title: Read Supabase Auth rate limits and enable leaked-password protection
actions.reason: Auth dashboard settings are not readable by the agent; advisor reports leaked password protection disabled.
actions.exactAction: Supabase → Authentication → Rate Limits: note the values. Authentication → Policies/Passwords: enable "Leaked password protection" (HaveIBeenPwned).

actions.title: Approve the league_memberships policy recursion fix
actions.reason: Direct SELECT on league_memberships by any signed-in user fails with 42P17 (infinite recursion) — in production and in repo 004_leagues.sql. Fails closed; app unaffected (uses RPCs).
actions.exactAction: Review supabase/pending/rc2-3-10-league-memberships-policy-recursion.sql; approve it for the next controlled production migration (PRODUCTION_MIGRATION_READY).

actions.title: Decide on production-only table public._jev_triage_tmp
actions.reason: 5 rows (request_id, feedback_id) left from a manual pg_net triage run; not in the repo; RLS on with no policy (no client access) but anon/authenticated hold table grants.
actions.exactAction: After OA-DATA-EXPORT: approve dropping public._jev_triage_tmp (or tell the agent why it must stay).
actions.risk: None for the app (no code reads it).

actions.title: Decide whether progress snapshots keep the account e-mail
actions.reason: 12 of 14 user_progress.client_snapshot rows carry account.email (written by supabaseLearningRepository.ts). Only the owner of the row can read it (RLS), but the e-mail already lives in auth.users.
actions.exactAction: Choose: keep (documented) or drop from new snapshots (code change in RC2.3.11+, existing rows rewritten on next sync).

actions.title: Run the cloud smoke after the next production deploy
actions.reason: Production hosts are unreachable from the agent session; the smoke runs from GitHub Actions with the seeded QA account.
actions.exactAction: GitHub → Actions → "Cloud smoke (manual, production)" → expected_sha = live SHA from OA-PROD-WEB-SHA.
actions.evidenceExpected: Run URL; artifact cloud-smoke-report shows PASS per step.

actions.title: Physical QA on the certified APK only
actions.reason: A physical test on an older APK cannot certify the current release.
actions.exactAction: Install the APK artifact of this PR head, open /qa/device?expect=<PR head SHA>, confirm MATCH before recording any physical result.

actions.title: Owner cloud acceptance
actions.reason: OWNER_CLOUD_ACCEPTANCE is only ever a person's signature.
actions.exactAction: When every RC2.3.10 gate is PASS, sign OWNER_CLOUD_ACCEPTANCE in docs/release/rc2-3-10-cloud-matrix.json (ownerSignature + date).
